summarySteps: 1. Calendar Spreads ([fact-01], [fact-02]): Sell short-dated T1 and buy long-dated T2 at strike K to exploit faster near-term theta decay across neutral, bullish, or bearish strikes.
2. Long Straddles ([fact-03], [fact-10]): Buy a European call and put at same strike K and maturity T, yielding terminal gross payoff |S_T - K| and requiring moves beyond total premium c + p.
3. Long Straddle Metrics ([fact-04], [fact-10]): For K = $50, call $4, put $3 ($7 total debit), downside break-even is $43, upside break-even is $57, and max loss is $700 at S_T = $50.
4. Short Straddles ([fact-05]): Sell a call and put at strike K, collecting maximum profit c + p if S_T = K but facing unlimited risk on large price movements.
5. Volatility Crush Risk ([fact-09]): Business Snapshot 11.2 highlights how pre-earnings IV surges and post-announcement collapses can crush option values despite large stock moves.
6. Strips and Straps ([fact-06]): Use strips (1 call, 2 puts) for bearish volatility views or straps (2 calls, 1 put) for bullish volatility views.
7. Bottom Strangles ([fact-07], [fact-11]): Buy OTM put K1 and OTM call K2 (K1 < K2) to lower initial cost, requiring larger underlying moves for profitability.
8. Strangle Metrics ([fact-08], [fact-11]): Strangle break-evens equal K2 + Net Debit and K1 - Net Debit, with maximum loss equal to net debit paid realized between K1 and K2.
bottomTakeaway: Advanced volatility strategies harness calendar time decay and multi-option straddles, strangles, strips, and straps, requiring careful management against implied volatility crush around earnings events ([fact-01], [fact-02], [fact-03], [fact-04], [fact-05], [fact-06], [fact-07], [fact-08], [fact-09]).
